title: HMAC accumulation buffer: O(N²) copy cost across multiple HmacUpdate calls
description: Each wc_HmacUpdate call allocates a new buffer of size (dataSz + inSz), copies all previous data into it, zeroes the old buffer, and frees it. For N calls of size M, total copy work is M + 2M + 3M + ... = O(N²M). In TLS Finished HMAC (2-3 small updates), this is irrelevant. For large HMAC inputs (e.g., bulk data MAC), each update doubles the allocation and copy overhead. Expected impact: visible for inputs over ~64KB in multiple calls; for 1MB HMAC in 64KB chunks, 16 calls = 16*8MB ≈ 128MB of copies. Fix direction: realloc semantics (grow buffer without copying if possible) or linked-list of chunks assembled at Final. The linked-list approach is simpler and avoids repeated kernel allocations.
